summary: Los Padres AWS post built 1942 and rebuilt 1943; its cabin moved to Marble Peak and was lost in the 1984 Gordo-Rat-Creek Fire. Site today not described.

facts.design: 1943 standard AWS post with a ground cabin and observation cupola; the 1942 first building was a small one-room cabin
facts.status_note: The cabin was moved to Marble Peak and later consumed in the 1984 Gordo-Rat-Creek Fire; no source describes the site now
facts.agency: US Forest Service - Los Padres National Forest

events.note: Small one-room building erected in mid-1942 for the Aircraft Warning Service (register); the history page says a small one-room cabin was constructed for the AWS
Harry and Lillian Ross staffed the post in mid-1942
Standard AWS post with a ground cabin and cupola replaced the original building
Cabin bought and moved to Marble Peak as a private summer retreat. The history page says the late 1940s; the register says some time in the 1950s. The year is approximate.
The moved cabin was consumed in the Gordo-Rat-Creek Fire. The register's removal field says 1984 - Wildfire for the site.

corrections.proposed: 1942 built (first one-room cabin); 1943 is the replacement standard post
corrections.why: Both sources date the first building to mid-1942 and describe the 1943 post as replacing it.

corrections.proposed: Cabin relocated to Marble Peak in the late 1940s or 1950s; the moved cabin was consumed in the 1984 fire
corrections.why: The register's removal field credits the 1984 wildfire with the site's loss, but both sources say the cabin had already been moved away before that fire.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says the cabin moved some time in the 1950s; the history page says it was bought and moved in the late 1940s. Both name Marble Peak, so only the date is in doubt.

notes_for_editor: Both pages draw on Lookouts of the Los Padres Forest (Reaves, 1988), so they are not independent sources. The brief's kind 'unknown' is a cabin on a post, not a tower. Two searches found nothing on what remains today, so the story says so. No access or visit facts were added because no source gives them. No photo added: the register's 1988 photo credit has no image URL in the cache.
